messages:
hao: heads up — CI red on main: linux-integ/runner-374 failing in allocator_test after merge of cache-refactor PR 4329. logs: https://ci.redwood/c/1234
CI Bot: Build failed on linux-integ/runner-374. Tests failing: allocator_test::shard_split (exit code 1). Logs uploaded: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/1234
maria: ack. can someone rerun CI? suspect cache-refactor but want a bisect if rerun flakes
samir: rerun queued: https://ci.redwood/c/1234/retry
jess: ran quick git blame. last green on main was commit 7a1f2b3 (2026-03-12). PR 4329 merged at 2026-03-13 02:11 UTC
ryan: pinging @eng-infra; can we start a bisect between 7a1f2b3..HEAD? I'll try a binary search on CI if someone gives tips for sharding the allocator test
hao: thanks. procedure: use `git bisect start HEAD 7a1f2b3` then run the failing test on the CI image locally with `./scripts/run_integ_allocator.sh` to reproduce. If you need an infra agent, @oncall-bot can attach a runner
oncall-bot: @ryan I'm attaching a debug runner to your workspace: debug-runner-21
samir: first rerun finished and failed reproducibly; capturing logs and adding to thread
samir: logs snippet: ```E allocator_shard.cc:345 Assertion failed: shard_count > 0```
jess: that assertion points at the kv-shard allocator path introduced in PR 4329. putting up a quick revert candidate on a branch
maria: if bisect shows PR 4329 as culprit we should revert asap. can someone volunteer to open the revert PR? I can do it if no one else
ryan: I'm running local bisect now, will post results. ETA ~30m
CI Bot: Bisect run started by ryan: https://ci.redwood/bisect/789
hao: note: if bisect is noisy, try running with `--runs 3` to reduce flake noise
ryan: bisect step 6/10 marked bad. currently narrowed down to range where PR 4317 and 4329 touch allocator code
samir: quick grep shows 4317 is unrelated (comment only). 4329 touches shard initialization. high suspect
jess: I'll prep a fast revert branch and run CI green check. If green, open revert PR and tag @release
maria: thanks. also leaving a note for postmortem if revert goes in
ryan: bisect finished: first bad commit = 6d4f9c2 (merge of PR 4329). confirming with `git show 6d4f9c2`
samir: confirm repro on debug-runner-21 with that commit
jess: revert PR opened: https://git.redwood/r/4543 Revert "kv cache refactor" — tagging @release @eng-sre
maria: nice. can we do a quick canary on dedicated before full revert? prefer to avoid churn
hao: safer to revert on main now, then rework PR 4329 in feature branch. Can revert and then promote dedicated later
maria: agreed. merging revert once CI passes on revert branch
CI Bot: CI passed on revert branch: https://ci.redwood/c/1256
jess: merged revert r/4543
hao: rolling back main to last green. please monitor for any residual flakes. I'll follow up with a brief postmortem draft
maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ryan: leaving bisect notes in the PR and assigning to author of 4329 to follow up
samir: closing bisect run https://ci.redwood/bisect/789/status: success
maria: tagging incident doc: https://wiki.redwood/incident/allocator-shard-2026-03-14
hao: done — assigning to @jess and @author-4329 for follow up
